title: Transfer of halted runs
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a state set, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let $M$ and $N$ be deterministic machines with $k$ work tapes and Boolean symbols, with $q_a\in S$. Suppose their transition actions agree in every state other than $q_a$, and in state $q_a$ machine $N$ takes the control action that stays on the input head and returns to $q_a$ without writing, moving work heads, or emitting output. If the run of $N$ from a configuration $c$ is halted after $T$ steps, then the run of $M$ from $c$ has the same configuration after $T$ steps, and at every time $j\le T$ its state is not $q_a$.
hypotheses_covered: $k$ is a natural number; state set $S$; Boolean input word $x$
Machines $M,N$ each have $k$ work tapes and Boolean symbols
Transition tables agree for every state $q\ne q_a$ and all scanned inputs/work symbols
At $q_a$, $N$ takes the stationary, silent control action returning to $q_a$ for all scanned inputs/work symbols
The run of $N$ from $c$ is halted at time $T$
replaced:
Let two transition tables agree away from an anchor state, which the second
(stopped) table turns into a silent self-loop. If the stopped run from $c$ is
halted at time $T$, then the active run from $c$ equals the stopped run at time
$T$, and the active run never visits the anchor at any time up to $T$.
